previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old woman with alcoholic cirrhosis was admitted due to melena and weakness. She had a history of esophageal varices and recent treatment for a urinary tract infection, though a repeat culture showed contamination. Initial labs showed stable hemoglobin at 11.7 g/dL and no signs of active infection or hepatic encephalopathy. An endoscopy revealed grade I esophageal varices and mild gastritis but no active bleeding. She was managed with IV pantoprazole and octreotide, then transitioned to oral omeprazole. Her hemoglobin declined slightly to 10.2 g/dL but remained stable without transfusion. Trazodone was discontinued due to concerns about polypharmacy and sedation. She was discharged home after two days in stable condition with instructions to follow up with her primary care provider, psychiatrist, and neurology, and to complete outpatient evaluations including a repeat endoscopy and cognitive assessment.
